shortDescription: Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 25, 2026) - Silver Elephant Mining Corp. TSX:ELEF (OTCQB: SILEF) (FSE: 1P2) ("Silver Elephant" or the "Company") is pleased to report laboratory assay results from the drill core verification program at its Robinson-Lasher zinc-germanium-galli…

children: is pleased to report laboratory assay results from the drill core verification program at its Robinson-Lasher zinc-germanium-gallium project (the "Robinson-Lasher Project" or the "Project") in Livingston County, Kentucky.

As mentioned in the Company's news release on October 14, 2026, forty-six spot samples from four archived drill holes at the Earth Analysis Research Library of the Kentucky Geological Survey in Lexington, Kentucky, were analyzed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry ("ICP-MS"). The results from holes DXHR-01 and DXHR-03 confirm high-grade zinc, with germanium and gallium, at drill core intervals that broadly match those recorded in 2008. The 2026 assay results returned notably higher silver grades than the 2008 assays.
Germanium (currently trading at $269/oz1) is hosted in the sphalerite, while gallium (trading at $97.22/oz2) is present both in the zinc and in the fluorspar mineralized zones.

Holes DXHR-02 and DXHL-01 did not contain significant germanium mineralized intervals in either the 2008 or the 2026 assay data. DXHL-01 was drilled to test for fluorspar beds and returned 61.8% CaF₂ over 8.0 feet in 2008.

Each 2026 assay sample is from a spot location: it shows the composition of the core at that point and does not represent the grade of an interval. The selected high germanium and silver results are set out in Table 1, which also displays the 2008 historical assays at the same depths for comparison purposes. Table 2 displays the full 2026 assay results. Drill hole details are set out in Table 3.
Table 1 - Best results: highest germanium and silver values, with 2008 historical assays at the same depths

The ten highest germanium values and the ten highest silver values, ranked by germanium. 2026 values are single spot samples; 2008 values are historical assays of the full interval shown. nil = below detection; n.a. = not analyzed. 1 g/t = 1 ppm. Depths are downhole; holes are vertical (−90°), so downhole intervals approximate true thickness.

The 2026 samples returned high-grade zinc within the 2008 zinc intervals. This includes 50.17% Zn at 580.0 feet, 49.23% Zn at 586.0 feet, and 39.70% Zn at 575.0 feet in DXHR-01, and 40.57% Zn at 630.0 feet and 38.35% Zn at 628.0 feet in DXHR-03. Samples between sphalerite bands returned zinc below the detection limit, as expected for spot samples in banded mineralized zones.

Germanium content tracks with zinc, with the highest values in the most zinc-rich samples: 215.4 g/t Ge correlates with 40.57% Zn (DXHR-03; 630 feet), 114.2 g/t Ge correlates with 38.35% Zn (DXHR-03; 628 feet), 115.4 g/t Ge correlates with 50.17% Zn (DXHR-01; 580 feet) and 85.8 g/t Ge correlates with 49.23% Zn (DXHR-01; 586 feet). This indicates that germanium is likely substituting within the sphalerite crystal structure, as described in the Company's July 6, 2026, news release.

Gallium is confirmed in both the zinc and fluorspar mineralized zones, with values of up to 25.7 g/t Ga at 217.0 feet in the fluorspar mineralized interval in DXHL-01, 16.2 g/t Ga at 628.0 feet and 13.5 g/t Ga at 630.0 feet in DXHR-03 in the zinc mineralized interval, and 14.1 g/t Ga at 523.0 feet in DXHR-02 in the zinc mineralized interval. These values are comparable to the 2008 analyses, which returned gallium of up to 20 g/t.
Silver correlates with zinc, with up to 23.2 g/t Ag at 630.0 feet in DXHR-03, and 20.3 g/t Ag at 580.0 feet and 15.0 g/t Ag at 639.0 feet in DXHR-01.
These two holes did not intersect the high-grade zinc found in DXHR-01 and DXHR-03, and each was analyzed for germanium and gallium for the first time.

DXHL-01 was drilled in 2008 to test for fluorspar beds at the base of the Bethel Sandstone, as opposed to the zinc horizon. The 2008 drill log recorded bedded fluorspar with no sphalerite, and the 2008 assays returned 61.8% CaF2 over 8.0 feet. The 2026 samples from this fluorspar bed returned gallium of up to 25.7 g/t.

DXHR-02 was drilled between DXHR-01 and DXHR-03 and intersected the Sub-Rosiclare zinc horizon. The 2008 assays returned 2.5% Zn over 8.0 feet from 504.0 feet. The 2026 samples returned 2.87% Zn with 3.2 g/t Ge and 0.4 g/t Ga at 511.3 feet, and 1.48% Zn with 3.5 g/t Ge and 14.1 g/t Ga at 523.0 feet.

High-grade zinc mineralization is confirmed in holes DXHR-01 and DXHR-03 within the intervals recorded in 2008, with values of up to 50.17% Zn.
Germanium is confirmed within the sphalerite mineralized zones, with values of up to 215.4 g/t Ge.
Gallium is confirmed in the zinc and in the fluorspar mineralized intervals, with values of up to 25.7 g/t Ga, which are comparable to the 2008 analyses.
Silver is prevalent throughout the zinc mineralized zones, occurring in every zinc-bearing sample, with values of up to 23.2 g/t Ag.
Following these results, the Company's priorities for the Robinson-Lasher Project are:
Completion of the independent NI 43-101 technical report by Mercator Geological Services Limited.
Compilation and validation of the historical database of 232 drill holes totaling over 100,000 feet.
Confirmation drilling on the Robinson structure, with continuous sampling of the mineralized zones for zinc, germanium and gallium.
Preliminary metallurgical test work to assess and maximize germanium and gallium recovery in zinc concentrate.

Readers are cautioned that no metallurgical test work, processing arrangement, mineral resource estimate or economic assessment has been completed on the Robinson-Lasher Project, and there is no certainty that germanium or gallium can be economically recovered.

Samples were cut from the archived core with a precision rotary tool at single depths, generally one to five feet apart, in accordance with the sampling policies of the Kentucky Geological Survey, which require that sufficient archive material be retained in each core box. The rotary tool bit was cleaned in an ultrasonic cleaner bath between each sample. Spot samples in banded sphalerite mineralization can return values well above or below the grade of the surrounding interval, and the Company has therefore not calculated interval grades from them.

Samples were analyzed by ICP-MS at the University of Kentucky Department of Plant and Soil Sciences, under the quality assurance and quality control protocol described in the Company's news release of October 14, 2026. Method detection limits were 0.25% Zn, 0.45 g/t Ge, 0.24 g/t Ga and 0.17 g/t Ag. Analytical results generated from repository material are provided to the Kentucky Geological Survey and become part of the public record of the collection.
